title: Class Interfaces and Responsibilities
learningObjectives: Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: A class interface describes what clients can do; its implementation contains how it works. Responsibilities should be cohesive and interfaces small.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear interfaces reduce coupling and make code easier to test and change.
understand.explain: Expose meaningful operations, hide details, and avoid classes that do too many unrelated things.

examples.title: Small interface
examples.code: class Counter{public:void increment(){++value;}int get()const{return value;}private:int value=0;};

examples.title: Hide implementation detail
examples.explanation: Clients use the getter rather than directly accessing data.

examples.title: Single responsibility
examples.code: class Timer{public:void reset(){seconds=0;}int elapsed()const{return seconds;}private:int seconds=0;};

examples.title: Validate interface
examples.code: class Score{public:bool set(int n){if(n<0||n>100)return false;score=n;return true;}private:int score=0;};

examples.title: Use public API
examples.explanation: Client code calls the public operation.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five Class Interfaces and Responsibilities examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating class interfaces and responsibilities in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

questions.explanation: Clients need not depend on internal details.
A small purposeful interface is easier to use.
Unrelated responsibilities make classes harder to maintain.
